newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court to hear final appeals on sleaze case.
newsitem.headline: French court to hear final appeals on sleaze case.

text.p: France's supreme court will hear on Tuesday a last-ditch appeal by Lyon's ex-mayor, the Cannes mayor and the country's most popular news broadcaster in a sleaze case symbolising tawdry 1980s links between politicians and business.

An appeals court in Lyon, France's second biggest city, gave former Lyon mayor Michel Noir and Cannes mayor Michel Mouillot suspended 18-month prison terms and hefty fines a year ago for their roles in illicit campaign funding schemes.

Also convicted of being an accomplice to misuse of corporate funds was Patrick Poivre d'Arvor, star broadcaster on the country's main TF1 television channel, who received a 15-month suspended sentence for accepting lavish gifts including Caribbean holidays.

Funds and gifts came from corporate funds embezzled by Noir's businessman son-in-law Pierre Botton. Botton, serving a three-and-a-half year sentence, has not appealed and was recently reported to have tried to take his life in prison.
Noir, Mouillot and Poivre d'Arvor have appealed to the supreme court (Cour de Cassation) on technicalities. The court cannot modify the sentences, but can either confirm them or order a re-trial.

If the sentences were confirmed, Noir, a member of parliament and a former trade minister once tipped as a possible presidential candidate, and Mouillot will be declared ineligible for public office for five years.

In a separate case, Noir is appealing against a 12-month suspended sentence for diverting eight million francs ($1.6 million) of Lyon's municipal funds to finance political campaigns and personal expenses.
Mouillot is in prison, awaiting trial in a separate case on accusations that he extorted money from casinos in his Riviera resort.
